proposals.before: After she married Dewu, within a year he was implicated in his cousin Jin Cai's crime and banished to the far south.
proposals.after: After she married Dewu, within a year he was implicated through his paternal uncle Jin Cai's affair and banished to the far south.
proposals.reason: Chinese 從父 denotes a paternal uncle, not a cousin; the idiomatic English misstates the kinship.

proposals.before: She married Dewu; after one year Dewu was implicated in his cousin Jin Cai's affair and exiled to Lingnan.
proposals.after: She married Dewu; after one year Dewu was implicated in his paternal uncle Jin Cai's affair and exiled to Lingnan.
proposals.reason: Literal English likewise renders 從父 as cousin; it should be paternal uncle.

proposals.before: Wuji's uncle by the father's line often held banquets for pleasure; Changze would sometimes attend, and Wuji killed him with a brick.
proposals.after: Wuji's father's elder cousin often held banquets for pleasure; Changze would sometimes attend, and Wuji killed him with a brick.
proposals.reason: 從伯 denotes a paternal elder cousin of the father, not a father's brother; the idiomatic rendering is correct.

proposals.before: At the slightest hint of persuasion she would weep and sob in grief; this happened again and again.
proposals.after: At the slightest hint of persuasion she would weep and sob in grief; this happened several times.
proposals.reason: 數四 means several times; 'again and again' overstates frequency versus the Chinese and the literal.

proposals.before: At eighteen Shangguan married Prince Lingui, succeeding as consort after the lamented King of Chu.
proposals.after: At eighteen Shangguan married Prince Lingui, who succeeded the lamented King of Chu.
proposals.reason: 繼楚哀王後 refers to Lingui continuing after King Ai of Chu, not to Shangguan succeeding as that king's consort.

proposals.before: When she was only a few years old, whenever her parents Quan fell ill she would observe their expressions, never leave their side, and attend them day and night like an adult.
proposals.after: When she was only a few years old, whenever her parents happened to fall ill she would observe their expressions, never leave their side, and attend them day and night like an adult.
proposals.reason: 權有疾 means 'happened to fall ill' / 'whenever ill'; 權 is not a personal name Quan.

proposals.before: Her father Keji was skilled in literary composition; during Empress Wu's reign he served as Vice Director of the Bureau of Astronomy.
proposals.after: Her father Keji was skilled in literary composition; during Empress Wu's reign he served as Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel (Heavenly Officials).
proposals.reason: 天官侍郎 under Wu Zhou is the Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel (天官=吏部), not the Bureau of Astronomy.

proposals.before: Her father Keji was skilled in literary composition; during Wu Zetian's reign he served as Vice Director of the Bureau of Astronomy.
proposals.after: Her father Keji was skilled in literary composition; during Wu Zetian's reign he served as Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel (Heavenly Officials).
proposals.reason: Same office mistranslation: 天官侍郎 is Ministry of Personnel, not astronomy.

proposals.before: During the Kaiyuan era Tingyu was repeatedly promoted to Regional Commander of Qingzhou.
proposals.after: During the Kaiyuan era Tingyu was repeatedly promoted to Regional Commander of Qing Prefecture (慶州).
proposals.reason: 慶州 is Qing Prefecture, not Qingzhou (青州); the idiomatic rendering is correct.

proposals.before: Earlier, when Zhang Yue was Chief Minister of the Secretariat, in his youth he had been valued by Keji; Wei resented that her husband held an outer post, so she wrote a letter to Yue recounting her late father's affairs of former days and pleading Tingyu's case, and enclosed the "Rhapsody on the Southern Expedition" to send to Yue.
proposals.after: Earlier, Chief Minister Zhang Yue had in his youth been valued by Keji; Wei resented that her husband held an outer post, so she wrote a letter to Yue recounting her late father's affairs of former days and pleading Tingyu's case, and enclosed the "Rhapsody on the Southern Expedition" to send to Yue.
proposals.reason: 中書令張說年少時為克己所重 means Zhang Yue (the Chief Minister) was valued by Keji when young, not that he already held that office in youth.

proposals.before: At the time Cao Sheng was promoted to Prefect of Xuzhou; learning the bandits had surrendered, he led troops in a surprise attack.
proposals.after: At the time Cao Sheng was Prefect of Xuzhou; learning the bandits had surrendered, he led troops in a surprise attack.
proposals.reason: 任 marks holding the office, not promotion; the idiomatic translation is accurate.

proposals.before: There was also Wang Fan's wife, Lady Pei, Assistant Magistrate of Weishi, daughter of Jujing, Tutor to the Prince of Yi.
proposals.after: There was also the wife of Wang Fan, Assistant Magistrate of Weishi, Lady Pei, daughter of Jujing, Tutor to the Prince of Yi.
proposals.reason: Chinese 尉氏尉王泛妻裴氏 makes Wang Fan the Assistant Magistrate of Weishi; the idiomatic English wrongly attaches that office to Lady Pei.

proposals.before: An edict stated, "The late Lu Fu, Assistant Magistrate of Yuanwu in Zheng Prefecture, whose wife was Lady Li, and the late Wang Fan, Assistant Magistrate of Weishi in Bian Prefecture, whose wife was Lady Pei, among others—exemplary virtue ran in their families, gentle clarity rooted in their nature;
proposals.after: An edict stated, "The late wife of Lu Fu, Assistant Magistrate of Yuanwu in Zheng Prefecture, née Li, and the late wife of Wang Fan, Assistant Magistrate of Weishi in Bian Prefecture, née Pei, among others—exemplary virtue ran in their families, gentle clarity rooted in their nature;
proposals.reason: Chinese 盧甫亡妻李氏 and 王泛亡妻裴氏 mark the wives as deceased, not the husbands; the idiomatic English reverses the 亡妻 construction.

proposals.before: I am now escorting four coffins and have reached Chang'an, lodging temporarily at an inn; I do not know where the tomb of the former Prince of Yue lies; I humbly beg Your Majesty to grant my petition and permit burial in the ancestral tomb.
proposals.after: I am now escorting four coffins and have temporarily lodged at an inn at Changle; I do not know where the tomb of the former Prince of Yue lies; I humbly beg Your Majesty to grant my petition and permit burial in the ancestral tomb.
proposals.reason: Chinese 長樂旅店 is an inn at Changle, not a generic arrival at Chang'an; the translation invents Chang'an for 長樂.

proposals.before: Now escorting four coffins, I have reached Chang'an and temporarily lodged at an inn; I do not know the location of the former Prince of Yue's tomb; I humbly beg Heaven's grace to grant my petition and permit return to the great tomb.
proposals.after: Now escorting four coffins, I have reached a Changle inn and lodged there temporarily; I do not know the location of the former Prince of Yue's tomb; I humbly beg Heaven's grace to grant my petition and permit return to the great tomb.
proposals.reason: Chinese 長樂旅店 denotes the Changle inn; rendering it as Chang'an misidentifies the place name.

decisions.after: After she married Dewu, within a year he was implicated in his paternal uncle Jin Cai's crime and banished to the far south.
decisions.reason: s0010 從父金才 is Dewu's paternal uncle Jin Cai, not a cousin; the kinship fix is required, but 'implicated through … affair' is awkward, so keep 'in … crime' and change only the kinship term.
s0010 從父 denotes paternal uncle; the literal's 'cousin' is wrong, and replacing it with 'paternal uncle' is accurate and natural.
s0092 從伯 is the father's elder paternal cousin, not a generic paternal uncle; the proposed wording matches the idiomatic sense and the Chinese.
s0070 數四 means a limited several times; 'again and again' overstates the frequency relative to the Chinese.
s0316 繼楚哀王後 follows 歸於靈龜 and marks Lingui as successor after King Ai of Chu, not Shangguan succeeding as that king's consort.
s0134 權有疾 means the parents happened to fall ill; 權 is adverbial, not a personal name Quan.
Under Wu Zhou, 天官 is the renamed Ministry of Personnel (吏部); 天官侍郎 is not an astronomy post.
Literal repeats the same 天官侍郎 error; Ministry of Personnel (Heavenly Officials) is the correct Wu Zhou office.

decisions.after: During the Kaiyuan era Tingyu was repeatedly promoted to Regional Commander of Qing Prefecture.
decisions.reason: s0182 慶州 is Qing Prefecture, not Qingzhou (青州); the proposed gloss is right, but the English replacement must not embed Chinese characters.
s0183 中書令張說年少時為克己所重 identifies Zhang Yue by later title while locating Keji's favor in Yue's youth, not during his chief ministership.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 中書令張說年少時為克己所重

decisions.reason: s0332 任徐州刺史 marks holding the prefecture, not a promotion; dropping 'promoted to' restores the sense.
s0214 尉氏尉王泛妻裴氏 attaches 尉氏尉 to Wang Fan; the original idiomatic wrongly makes Lady Pei the Assistant Magistrate.
s0220 盧甫亡妻李氏 and 王泛亡妻裴氏 mark the wives as deceased; the idiomatic reverse attribution to the husbands is wrong.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 盧甫亡妻李氏、汴州尉氏縣尉王泛亡妻裴氏

decisions.reason: s0282 長樂旅店 is an inn at Changle; 長安 Chang'an is a different place name invented by the idiomatic rendering.
Literal likewise misreads 長樂旅店 as Chang'an; Changle inn is the correct place.

claimRevisions.reason: Accepted r0013 shows 亡妻 marks Lady Li as the deceased wife, not a widow of a late husband; restore kinship term and end-state from the Chinese.
